key_insight: Per-chip activation cuts row-activation energy ~8-16x for random 8-64 B gathers (graph, KV); real value only with a custom DIMM/RCD routing per-chip CA.
killer_doubt: Standard DIMMs share CA/CS per rank (PDA is MRS-only), so 'existing DIMMs' fails; a 64 B line from one x4 chip needs BL128 = 20 ns burst and breaks chipkill.
decisive_experiment: Largely settled in literature. If pursued: FPGA board with 16 discrete x4 DDR5 parts on per-chip CA, replay graph/KV traces, measure pJ per useful bit vs a DDR5 subchannel baseline (~$150k).
prior_art: Mini-rank (Zheng, MICRO 2008); MC-DIMM rank subsetting (Ahn); Rambus threaded module; SSA (Udipi, ISCA 2010); DDR5 32-bit subchannels.

key_insight: Tier-granular remap makes random tier defects yield-neutral: a correct design rule every 3D-DRAM dossier should carry, not a standalone invention.
killer_doubt: At 0.01 defects/tier/die over 1,000 blocks, one spare tier per block gives 99.95% die yield; 20% overbuild adds ~20% etch depth. Loosened windows cause systematic, unsparable defects.
decisive_experiment: Desk yield model (<$50k) on published tier-defect data: 1-2 spare tiers per block plus vertical-bitline column sparing vs 20% overbuild; list defect classes (vertical BL shorts) tier sparing cannot fix.
prior_art: 3D NAND spare blocks and word lines with bad-block tables; DRAM row/column redundancy; SK hynix 5-tier 3D DRAM at 56.1% yield.

key_insight: A crystalline channel is the real CTE fix (Si CCDs reach ~0.99999). Workaround: rotate it, horizontal CCDs in epi Si/SiGe 3D-DRAM stacks, vertical gate pillars as shared phases.
killer_doubt: No single-crystal Si fills 128-tier holes; poly-Si grain-boundary generation (~100-1000x bulk) cuts 85 C hold from ~3 s (crystalline, ~120 e-/s/well) to ~3-30 ms.
decisive_experiment: Planar 16-gate surface-channel CCD on SOI vs on laser-crystallized poly-Si at a university fab (~$200k): measure CTE at 0.1-1 GHz clocks and dark generation per well at 85 C.
prior_art: 1970s Si CCD memories; epitaxial Si/SiGe stacks for 3D DRAM (Samsung, imec). Vertical CCD memory: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Binary data with regenerating readout tolerates ~0.99-0.997 CTE per 64-128-transfer pass, not imaging's 0.9999; IGZO's >3 eV gap removes dark charge. Capacitor-free, transistor-free 3D bit.
killer_doubt: Plane-shared clocks shift every string in a block, so each needs its own sense path: per-row slits roughly halve density (4-8x to 2-4x 1b); 5 mm word-plane RC ~160 ns.
decisive_experiment: Planar overlapping-gate IGZO/IGO CCD, 16-32 gates, university fab (~$300k): CTE vs clock (10 MHz-1 GHz), fat zero, 85 C hold. Kill if per-transfer loss exceeds 3e-3 at 100 MHz.
prior_art: Phase B N-08 (same concept, ALIVE-SPEC); 1970s Si CCD memories; oxide-channel or vertical CCD memory: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Striping one cache line across 512 strings turns serial shifting into a fixed-latency parallel burst; floating-diffusion gain makes ~0.1 fF (~600 e-) wells enough.
killer_doubt: 200 tiers means up to ~400 transfers per pass: at 3e-3 loss per transfer only 30% survives, and 100-200 ns serial access far exceeds DRAM tRC (~45 ns).
decisive_experiment: Add 400-transfer recirculating loops to the I-01064 planar IGZO CCD chip: measure cumulative loss and pattern-dependent trailing charge, and set the maximum usable string length.
prior_art: Duplicate of Phase B N-08 and I-01064; 3D NAND word-plane stack as host. Vertical CCD memory: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Latch the whole string into SRAM (~20 ns) and write back in reverse (LIFO) order; 8 tiers need only ~16 transfers, so CTE ~0.99 suffices. Fold into I-01064.
killer_doubt: Density collapses: a gate-all-around CCD hole needs ~150 nm hex pitch (0.0195 um2), so 8 bits per hole is 0.0024 um2/bit, ~2x worse than 1b DRAM (0.0011).
decisive_experiment: Desk layout study (~$30k): bits/um2 vs string length for 60-150 nm hole pitch including per-row slits and sense paths; then add the LIFO latch scheme to the I-01064 test chip.
prior_art: 1970s CCD memories (serial latency killed them); LIFO write-back is standard shift-register practice. Vertical CCD memory: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: Ganging every third tier onto one of 3 clock phases needs ~3 contacts per block instead of a 128-step staircase; that staircase saving is the genuinely new cost lever.
killer_doubt: Duplicate of I-01064/N-08. Tier ganging needs selective plane contact (alternating plane metals), and the >10x fewer cleans/CMP per bit water claim is unquantified.
decisive_experiment: Fold into I-01064: on 8-16-plane test stacks, make one via that contacts only phase-1 planes after selective lateral recess of phase-2/3 planes (~$100k at a partner line).
prior_art: Duplicate of Phase B N-08 and I-01064; the 3D NAND staircase is the baseline it removes. Vertical CCD memory: none found (via search snippet).

key_insight: The read side works: a 64-cell IGZO series string (~10-15 kOhm/cell, ~0.5-1 uA) swings a 100 fF short bitline 50 mV in ~10 ns, with NAND-style pass-voltage bypass.
killer_doubt: Topology: the outer word plane gates only the outermost layer, so a write transistor between storage node and inner write bitline has no gate; it reverts to a floating-gate cell.
decisive_experiment: Planar first (~$250k, university fab): 16-cell series string of dual-gate IGZO 2T0C, read margin vs pass-gate Vt spread at 85 C; TCAD a gate-able 3D write-path topology before any vertical build.
prior_art: 3D NAND pass-voltage read; stacked and vertical IGZO 2T0C (imec, IME-CAS); Phase B N-43 coaxial 2T0C. NAND-string 2T0C: none found.

key_insight: Fixed-model weights in via ROM need no refresh, capacitor or EUV and can sit in logic BEOL beside compute, removing weight traffic entirely for frozen models.
killer_doubt: Via ROM at 64 nm pitch is 0.0041 um2/bit per deck, ~4x worse than 1b DRAM; BEOL offers ~4-5 tight decks; maskless e-beam writing ~1e10 vias/cm2 lacks production throughput.
decisive_experiment: Desk cost model (~$20k): $/bit for via ROM in 12-28 nm BEOL with 2 custom via masks vs DDR5 at $1.48/GB, including model-churn write-off every 6-12 months.
prior_art: Mask/via-programmable ROM (decades old); hardwired-weight inference ASICs from startups, e.g. Taalas (recollection, not verified this session).

key_insight: A face-to-face DRAM wafer under a wafer-scale engine gives ~3.9 TB at <0.3 pJ/bit with no TSV signal path; the processor's tile redundancy already absorbs DRAM tile defects.
killer_doubt: Power and cooling need opposite faces: ~20 kW at 0.8 V is ~25 kA through DRAM TSVs; W2W voids at ~0.1/cm2 (estimate) leave ~70 dead regions per wafer pair.
decisive_experiment: D2W hybrid-bond a DRAM test die face-to-face onto a 28 nm logic die at 2-6 um pitch, thinned (~$350k); measure bond yield, pJ/bit and 105 C retention under a 0.5 W/mm2 heater.
prior_art: Phase B N-41 carrier-is-memory (includes wafer-scale variant); Cerebras WSE (SRAM only); Graphcore Bow WoW (power wafer, not DRAM); imec/EVG W2W bonding.

key_insight: With stored electrons as avalanche seeds (trigger p~0.5), 40 electrons give 1e-12 miss probability: the physical floor is ~100 e- per bit, ~170x below today's 17,700.
killer_doubt: CMOS SPADs need guard rings at ~1-2 um pitch, ~900x a 1b cell; sharing one per bitline re-dilutes 100 e- to 0.46 mV on 35 fF; ~1% afterpulsing.
decisive_experiment: SPAD/CIS MPW (~$200k): 20 aF pinned storage wells transferring into shared SPADs; measure miss and false-fire rates vs electrons stored, dark counts and afterpulsing at 85 C.
prior_art: SPAD and quanta image sensors count single electrons; Phase B N-04 charge-transfer sensing reaches ~0.5 fF without avalanche. SPAD-read memory: none found.

key_insight: Equipotential guarding is sound: subthreshold leakage scales with 1-exp(-Vds/kT), so holding the mid node within 0.5 mV of the storage node would cut it ~50x.
killer_doubt: In-cell source followers carry Vgs ~0.4 V and ~20 mV mismatch: 20 mV residual gives only ~1.9x, and 1 nA follower bias per cell is ~1 A per Gb.
decisive_experiment: 28 nm MPW eDRAM macro (~$150k): 3T vs bootstrapped 5T cells, 1 Mb retention distributions at 85 C. Kill if tail gain <10x at <1.5x area with zero static bias.
prior_art: Electrometer guards; bootstrapped sample-and-hold switches; Giterman/Teman 4T feedback gain cells (~2016-18); IGZO access transistors already reach ~1 aA.
